diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..205606cda7db2a8c3cc4b489f105f19108b62c02 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -360,6 +360,9 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are if the
+    string also contains lowercase letters.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,13 +373,42 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
-        r"\b('?\w)",
-        lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
-        humanize(underscore(word)).title()
-    )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        # There is no telling acronyms from other words in an all-caps string
+        # like "HELLO WORLD", so it is titleized as it always has been. Such
+        # a string has no humps for underscore() to split, so lowercasing it
+        # is all that is needed before humanize().
+        return re.sub(
+            r"\b('?\w)",
+            lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
+            humanize(word.lower()).title()
+        )
+
+    def capitalize(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        apostrophe, part = match.groups()
+        # Keep words in capitals, like "NASA" or "DON'T", but not a capital
+        # after an apostrophe in a word that isn't, like "David'S".
+        if part.isupper() and (
+                not apostrophe or match.string[match.start() - 1].isupper()):
+            return match.group()
+        part = part.lower().title()
+        if apostrophe:
+            part = part[0].lower() + part[1:]
+        return apostrophe + part
+
+    # The same as humanize(underscore(word)), except that the case is kept
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = word.replace("-", "_")
+    word = re.sub(r"_[iI][dD]$", "", word)
+    word = word.replace("_", " ")
+    return re.sub(r"\b('?)(\w+)", capitalize, word)

description: the all-caps branch of titleize uses humanize(word.lower()) instead of humanize(underscore(word)), so hyphens and digit-capital boundaries are not handled as at base: titleize('X-MEN: THE LAST STAND') == 'X-Men: The Last Stand' and titleize('WI-FI') == 'Wi-Fi' instead of base 'X Men: The Last Stand' / 'Wi Fi'
